answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 17 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival forfeits the most. The island multiplier is published, charged in basalt, and tundra lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4795 identities would post 3506 proofs and burn roughly 6 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
